values.note: $20 a night, with the fee and registration procedure posted at the campground kiosk. A Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry to every state forest campground.

values.note: Drinking water from a hand-pump well. Boat launch.

values.note: All sites take tents and small trailers (the DNR's standard wording); some take 30-ft trailers/vehicles. Sites 1-11 are on Big Leverentz Lake, 12-18 on Little Leverentz Lake. One camping unit and six people per site.

sites.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/leverentzlake ('All sites will accommodate tents and small trailers, but some sites can accommodate 30-foot trailers/vehicles.' 'sites 1-11 on Big Leverentz Lake and sites 12-18 on Little Leverentz Lake'; 'One camping unit and six people are allowed per site') + amenity table (18 campsites), read 2026-10-25

values.note: Campground roads may not be plowed in winter.

season.source: https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table (Leverentz Lake State Forest Campground: 'Seasonal closure dates*' 'open all year'; '*Please note: SFCG campground roads may not be plowed in the winter'), read 2026-10-25

note: Secluded rustic state forest campground in two sections on Big and Little Leverentz Lakes (sites 1-11 on Big Leverentz, 12-18 on Little Leverentz), 2.7 mi E of Baldwin via US-10 and Forest Drive (Lake County); managed by the DNR Baldwin Field Office. Big Leverentz has the boat launch and a 50-ft floating dock; the Sheep Ranch Pathway is reached from both sections. --Claude
